response.reasons: Because if each gamble is "equally as attractive" as I was asked to make them, then inherently I cannot have a strong preference for either in choosing this choice, as they are "equally attractive" gambles. The concept that being told "the outcome of a gamble you might not have taken" is asinine, there is no gamble if I didn't take it. Statistically, you're telling me an "answer" is a fundamental lie.

trials.reasons: Because if each gamble is "equally as attractive" as I was asked to make them, then inherently I cannot have a strong preference for either in choosing this choice, as they are "equally attractive" gambles. The concept that being told "the outcome of a gamble you might not have taken" is asinine, there is no gamble if I didn't take it. Statistically, you're telling me an "answer" is a fundamental lie.

response.feedback: I think a gamble is the wrong framing for this question. There is no "outcome of a gamble you did not take" as random chance is random in the moment the choice is made. If I made a choice, then that is when that choice's random outcome occurs. If I did NOT make that choice, and you then spin the wheel, that is inherently a different wheel in a different moment in time than what I would have spun had I chosen THAT gamble.
